owner: the colour agent (Phase A seed by the colours builder)
tool: tools/colour.py (see tools/colours-README.md); never edit hex values by hand

rules.space: OKLab (Björn Ottosson 2020); hex values are 8-bit sRGB; distance() is Euclidean in OKLab (delta E OK)
rules.why: 0.10 in OKLab is about five just-noticeable differences (one is roughly 0.02 here), the point at which two fills separated by a thin outline read as different colours at a glance. Measured with this tool: Tableau 10's closest pair (teal and grey) is 0.084 and its median pair 0.185; ColorBrewer Pastel1's closest pair is 0.044. On this wheel, hues 15 degrees apart at one lightness sit 0.025-0.038 apart, 60 degrees apart 0.10-0.13, and the three lightness variants of one hue 0.10 (light/mid) and 0.12 (mid/deep), so 0.10 means: a different hue family, or a clearly different lightness. The vassal tint sits 0.12-0.15 from its suzerain's colour, so it is always told from the state itself; the contested blend sits half the pair's distance (0.05 at the minimum) from each claimant, which is why it carries a hatch. Capacity: the 72-colour wheel holds 17 mutually distinct colours at 0.10 (22 at 0.08, 10 at 0.12, 7 at 0.14), and the greedy colouring of the 1,129 polities without a fixed colour over the union of all 120 anchor years' adjacency (plus the polity table's 25 km neighbours) clears 0.10 for every polity and 0.12 for all but 3, then fails for 43 at 0.14 and 130 at 0.16. The 415 fixed conventional colours were tuned by hand until every neighbouring pair in every anchor year cleared 0.10; at 0.12, 57 neighbouring pairs of the conventional palette would fall short (Hungary beside Romania, Spain beside the Papal States, the Avars beside Lombard Italy), so 0.12 would cost about a fifth of the conventions. Every fixed and wheel colour also keeps at least 0.107 from the neutral grey and 0.18 from a pale basemap.
rules.neighbour: two polities are neighbours in a year when they own land cells that share an H3 edge (grid_ring(cell, 1)); the check runs over every anchor year, and later over every compiled year; a clash is resolved by recolouring the smaller state everywhere, so the colour-for-life rule holds
rules.lifetime: one colour per polity for its whole life; a dynasty change within a state keeps the colour; a successor that claims continuity takes a neighbouring hue of the same family; an unrelated successor takes an unrelated one; rows of one Cliopatria state (fixed entries sharing a group) share the colour
rules.readability: every fixed and wheel colour keeps OKLab L between 0.40 and 0.86 and chroma at least 0.03 (0.06 for hues), so each fill reads on the pale basemap (L about 0.95) and none is mistaken for the neutral grey

vassal.outline: the vassal's own colour (the suzerain's full colour) at 1 px
vassal.label: its own label
vassal.note: tint(hex, 'vassal'): OKLCH chroma x0.55, lightness +0.12; a vassal tint sits 0.12 to 0.14 from its suzerain's colour

occupied.note: occupied land is the occupier's colour hatched over the owner's; it becomes the occupier's only if annexed

contested.fill: blend(a, b): the OKLab midpoint of the two claimants (blue and red give purple)

hatch.colour: tint(fill, 'hatch'): the fill darkened by 0.18 L

contested.note: a fine diagonal hatch so the blend also reads for colour-blind viewers; the zone merges into the winner's full colour when the contest ends

rebel.fill: the rebel state's own colour at the vassal tint
rebel.note: rebel-held land is hatched in the rebels' own colour until they win (a new state keeps the rebel colour; a restoration keeps the old one) or are crushed

neutral.name: warm neutral grey
neutral.note: nobody's land: hunter-gatherers, stateless peoples, unorganised land; never blank

dots.colour: the culture's assigned colour at full chroma

culture.note: tint(hex, 'culture'): a desaturated pastel with a dotted fill, labelled as a culture, not a state

expansion_outline.colour: tint(hex, 'outline'): the state's colour darkened by 0.12 L at chroma x1.3
expansion_outline.duration: the first year the land is held

label.colour: tint(hex, 'label'): the state's colour at L -0.30 (not below 0.22), chroma x0.9

rules.basemap: no modern borders or labels: land, water, rivers and relief only, so the state colours are the only colours on the map

americas.note: national colours: USA navy-indigo, Canada red, Mexico green, Brazil green, Argentina light blue, Colombia blue, Venezuela light blue, Chile blue, Peru red; Inca terracotta, Aztec jade

africa.note: the Sahel empires gold and ochre, Songhai red-brown, Kush ochre-brown, Axum olive, Ethiopia gold, South Africa gold; Bornu magenta (320) and Nigeria green (150) are the exceptions

egypt.note: pharaonic Egypt sand gold, the Ptolemies lighter gold; modern Egypt burnt orange (50)

near-east.note: Sumer clay ochre, Akkad and Assyria red-brown, Lydia gold, Armenia orange, Palmyra desert gold; Babylon blue (265), Hittites magenta-violet (320), Phoenicia Tyrian purple (335) and Carthage Punic purple-indigo (285), Israel blue (250) and Jerusalem pale rose (345) by convention

light.use: the densest regions: minor states of the Holy Roman Empire, the taifas, the Warring States, the Rus principalities

wheel.note: assign prefers the variant its crowding rule gives a polity and falls back to the others; a colour is never reused for two polities that touch in any anchor year when the wheel has room
